for context:
full drop-in package in My Profile/echoclaim-spine/ (16 Python modules, all compiling, + docs, CI gate, and ZIH SLURM scripts).
The call, recapped: extend EchoClaim rather than build fresh. It's already a near-flagship in a German-insurance domain; the only real gap vs. your interview list was the operational spine, so that's what this adds.
What's in the package:

BUILD_PLAN.md — the master brief. Architecture, the zero-downtime migration design, eval methodology, LLMOps, ZIH usage, a PR-by-PR roadmap (PR1→PR7), an interview-question→code map (covers ~your whole list), and STAR resume bullets. This is the "no missing context" doc.
spine/retrieval/ — RAG over the policy corpus: structure-aware chunker, version-stamped embedder, Qdrant named-vector index, retriever+reranker, coverage_lookup Gemini tool, precision@k/nDCG eval, and migrate.py (the zero-downtime re-index centerpiece).
spine/llmops/ — prompt registry, LLM-judge groundedness, CI eval gate, PII-redacted trace logging, drift monitor.
README.md (rewritten, de-hackathoned) + DEHACKATHON_CHECKLIST.md — exact deletions/renames for the docs I can't see (kills the "verified facts April 2026" table, bounty/pitch/H0–H24 framing, the AI build-journal — the things that read as hackathon/AI-generated).

Recommended next step: do the actual in-repo wiring in Claude Code — open the repo, hand it BUILD_PLAN.md as the brief and spine/ as the scaffold, and run PR1→PR4 first (retrieval + migration carry the most interview weight). A 96-commit repo with telephony/voice is better edited in-place there than copied piecemeal.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

submission, and remove the tells that make docs look AI-generated. The rewritten
`README.md` in this package already does this for the front page; below is everything
else. I can't see these files from here, so this is a precise to-do list (do it in the
repo, or have Claude Code apply it).

## 1. Delete (pure hackathon/submission artifacts)

- `OPERATION_TURING_ADJUSTER_v2.md` — the "game plan" doc.
- `SUBMISSION_MANUAL.md` and `sumbission_manual.md` — submission instructions (the second
  is also a misspelled duplicate; remove both).
- `docs/entire-dispatches/` — the AI build-journal dispatches.
- Any `docs/ENTIRE.md` section whose purpose is the "Entire bounty" narrative.

## 2. Rename / neutralize

- Drop the codename framing "Operation: Turing Adjuster — Jamie" everywhere → just
  "EchoClaim" / "Jamie".
- `docs/SEQUENTIAL_RUNBOOK.md` → keep the technical bring-up order, delete the
  hour-by-hour ("H0–H4 …") hackathon timeline and the per-checkpoint race framing. Retitle
  to `docs/SETUP.md`.
- `tests/juror_bot.py` — the adversarial harness is good engineering; keep it, but rename

  at the eval gate (`llmops/eval_gate.py`) as a CI input.
- `aikido.yml` — keep (it's a real security CI gate); just remove any comment that frames
  it as "for the Aikido €1000 bounty".

## 3. Remove the "verified facts (April 2026)" table from any doc

That table ("hopeful claims that turned out not to match the docs…") is the single
biggest AI-generated tell. Replace with a normal, present-tense **Stack** section that
just states what's used (see the new README). Keep any genuinely useful "gotcha" as a
one-line note in the relevant module's README, phrased neutrally
(e.g. "The `gradium` package exposes `GradiumClient`, not `Client`.").

## 4. Strip bounty/pitch/marketing language repo-wide

Search and neutralize these terms wherever they appear in docs and comments:

```

juror|operation turing|pitch line|sweep|side-effect of the architecture|H[0-9]+–H[0-9]+" .
```

- Remove "sweeping the … bounties as a side-effect" and "the pitch line: …" sentences.
- Remove credit/prize amounts ("€1000", "900k credits", "Mac Mini").
- Replace "we built a voice agent that already knows the caller" hero tagline with the
  plain one-line description in the new README (or drop it).

## 5. Tone pass (de-AI)

- Cut em-dash-heavy dramatic asides and "the single tightest summary:" / "everything …;
  everything …; everything …" triadic flourishes. State things plainly.
- Remove bold-everywhere emphasis; keep bold for true keywords only.
- Prefer present tense and concrete nouns over hype ("low-latency loop", "resilience
  layers" → say what they actually are).
- Make commit messages going forward boring and descriptive; the migration/LLMOps PRs in
  `BUILD_PLAN.md` are a good place to establish that style.

## 6. Keep (these are strengths, not hackathon cruft)

  CI gate, the fallback chain, and the text-mode demo. These are exactly what a reviewer
  wants to see — just described in a neutral voice.

87	## 3. Design decisions (the interview answers, baked into code)
88	
89	### 3.1 Chunking — structure-aware, not fixed-length
90	Insurance policies and regulation (VVG, GDV model conditions, tariff docs) are
91	*hierarchical*: parts → sections (§) → clauses → sub-clauses. Fixed 512-token windows
92	shred a clause across chunks and destroy retrievability. Strategy:
93	- Primary split on document structure (headings / § markers / numbered clauses).
94	- Secondary split only when a clause exceeds a max-token budget, with overlap.
95	- Each chunk keeps metadata: `doc_id, section_path, clause_id, doc_type, product_code, lang`.
96	- This metadata is the payload Qdrant filters on (e.g. restrict to the caller's tariff).
97	
98	*Answers:* "What's your chunking strategy — length, semantics, or structure?"
99	
100	### 3.2 Vector DB — Qdrant
101	Chosen over Chroma (great for prototypes, weaker filtering/ops) and pgvector (fine if
102	you're already on Postgres, weaker ANN ergonomics at scale). Qdrant gives:
103	- **Payload filtering** (tariff/product/lang) co-indexed with vectors — essential here.
104	- **Named vectors** in one collection → two embedding versions side by side, which is
105	  what makes the zero-downtime migration clean.
106	- Runs free locally in Docker; same API self-hosted on a server later.
107	
108	*Answers:* "How do you choose a vector DB?" and "What's the right database for this task?"
109	(Note the contrast with `DataWhisper-AI`, which deliberately uses **no** vector DB —
110	NL→MongoDB structured queries. Keep that as the "when NOT to use vectors" example.)
111	
112	### 3.3 Embeddings — multilingual, version-stamped
113	**BGE-M3** (multilingual, strong on German; dense + sparse + ColBERT-style multi-vector
114	if wanted). The corpus and callers are German; an English-only model would tank recall.
115	Every vector is written with the embedding **model id + dimension** recorded on the
116	collection/version, so nothing is ambiguous when a second model appears.
117	
118	*Answers:* "How do embeddings work?" and feeds the migration story below.
119	
120	### 3.4 Zero-downtime embedding migration — the centerpiece
121	The scenario: *"Your embedding model changes — how do you migrate safely?"* Plan:
122	1. **Versioned by construction.** Vectors live under a named vector (`emb_v1`). The
123	   pipeline records `embedding_version` in payload and on a small `index_meta` record.
124	2. **Dual-write.** When `emb_v2` is introduced, new ingests write *both* `emb_v1` and
125	   `emb_v2`. Reads still serve `emb_v1`.
126	3. **Backfill.** A batch job re-embeds the existing corpus into `emb_v2` (this is the
127	   **ZIH GPU job** — see §6). Idempotent, resumable, checkpointed.
128	4. **Shadow eval.** Run `retrieval/eval.py` against both `emb_v1` and `emb_v2` on the
129	   golden set. Only proceed if `emb_v2` is non-inferior (within tolerance) or better on
130	   precision@k / nDCG.
131	5. **Atomic cutover.** Flip the active version (alias / config flag) so reads serve
132	   `emb_v2`. No downtime — both vectors were already present.
133	6. **Rollback.** Flip back instantly; `emb_v1` is still there until you GC it.
134	
135	*Answers:* "Can you update/backfill embeddings with zero downtime?" and Real-World
136	Scenario #1 end to end.
137	
138	### 3.5 Reranking + citation
139	Bi-encoder recall (top-50) → **bge-reranker-v2-m3** cross-encoder → top-k. Every
140	returned chunk carries `section_path / clause_id`, so the agent answer cites the exact
141	clause ("covered under §4(2) of KK-300"). Groundedness is then *checkable*, which the
142	LLM-judge does.
143	
144	*Answers:* reranking, citation, and the hallucination-monitoring story.
145	
146	### 3.6 Retrieval evaluation
147	`retrieval/eval.py` computes **precision@k, recall@k, MRR, nDCG@k** against a golden
148	set of `query → relevant clause_ids`. The golden set is bootstrapped by generating
149	question/answer pairs *from* the corpus clauses (synthetic, then spot-checked), which is
150	free and reproducible.
151	
152	*Answers:* "How do you evaluate retrieval quality?"
153	
154	### 3.7 LLMOps — what actually differs from classic MLOps
155	- **Prompt registry:** every prompt is a versioned artifact (semver + content hash).
156	  The running agent loads `jamie_system@<version>`; logs record which version produced
157	  each response. No more "we changed the prompt and quality moved, no idea when."
158	- **CI eval gate (`.github/workflows/llm-eval.yml`):** on any change to prompts, model
159	  config, or retrieval, CI runs the eval suite and **fails the merge** if precision@k,
160	  groundedness, or extraction F1 drop beyond a threshold. *This is the key CI/CD-for-LLM
161	  difference:* you gate on **probabilistic eval metrics and an LLM-judge**, not on
162	  deterministic unit assertions. Tests are non-flaky-by-design via fixed seeds, a frozen
163	  eval set, and tolerance bands rather than exact-match.
164	- **Logging middleware:** wraps the Gemini call; persists `{trace_id, prompt_version,
165	  retrieved_ids, response, judge_scores, latency, token_counts}` — PII-redacted via the
166	  existing `agent/pii_redact.py` — to SQLite/Parquet for audit and debugging. In a
167	  regulated insurance context this is a feature, not overhead.
168	- **Drift + hallucination monitor:** rolling windows over groundedness rate, retrieval
169	  score distribution, and extraction F1; flags drift (e.g. groundedness < 0.9 sustained).
170	
171	*Answers:* the whole MLOps/LLMOps cluster + "log prompts/outputs for debugging and
172	auditing" + "monitor performance drift or hallucinations" + the debugging-session
173	scenario (#7.4 — you now have the traces to do it).
174	
175	### 3.8 Cost & latency
176	- **Quantize GLiNER2** (ONNX + int8 dynamic quantization) for serving; `extraction/
177	  benchmark.py` already produces F1/latency/cost — extend it to include the quantized
178	  variant. *Answers:* "when should you quantize?"
179	- **Caching:** embedding cache (content hash → vector), retrieval cache (query hash →
180	  results), and an optional semantic response cache. *Answers:* batching + caching.
181	- **Context compression:** rerank then keep top-k and trim each chunk to the relevant
182	  span before it enters the prompt → fewer tokens. *Answers:* "reduce token usage" and
183	  "cheaper without killing quality" (#7.3).
184	- **Hosted vs OSS:** Gemini Flash for the live conversational turn (latency + quality);
185	  OSS local models (embedder, reranker, GLiNER2) for everything offline/high-volume.
186	  *Answers:* "when to use hosted APIs vs open-source models?"
187	
188	### 3.9 Determinism & fallback
189	- Structured outputs (the 15 pillars / 5 fraud signals) use constrained extraction
190	  (GLiNER2) rather than free-form generation → deterministic where it must be.
191	- The existing model fallback chain extends to a **retrieval fallback**: if Qdrant is
192	  unavailable or returns low-confidence, fall back to Tavily, then to a "I'll note that
193	  and a specialist will confirm" safe response — never hallucinate coverage.
194	*Answers:* "make the system more deterministic and less brittle" + "fallback if the LLM
195	fails mid-task".
196	
197	---
198	
199	## 4. PR-by-PR roadmap
200	
201	Each PR is independently mergeable and demoable. Acceptance criteria are the interview
202	talking points.
203	
204	| PR | Scope | Key files | Acceptance criteria |
205	|----|-------|-----------|---------------------|
206	| **PR1** | Corpus + structure-aware ingest + Qdrant index | `retrieval/{config,chunker,embedder,index}.py` | Corpus ingested; `index_meta` records embedding version; chunks carry section/clause metadata |
207	| **PR2** | Retriever + reranker + `coverage_lookup` tool wired into agent | `retrieval/{retriever,rerank,tool}.py`, `agent/` glue | Jamie can answer a coverage question with a cited clause in the text-mode demo |
208	| **PR3** | Retrieval eval + golden set | `retrieval/eval.py`, `spine/eval/golden_set.jsonl` | `precision@k / recall@k / MRR / nDCG` printed; numbers reproducible with a fixed seed |
209	| **PR4** | Zero-downtime migration | `retrieval/migrate.py` | Introduce `emb_v2`, dual-write, backfill, shadow-eval, atomic swap, rollback — all demoable, no read downtime |
210	| **PR5** | Prompt registry + CI eval gate | `llmops/{prompt_registry,judge,eval_gate}.py`, `.github/workflows/llm-eval.yml` | Prompt changes run CI eval; a deliberately worse prompt **fails** the gate |
211	| **PR6** | Logging middleware + drift monitor | `llmops/{logging_middleware,drift_monitor}.py` | Every turn logged (PII-redacted) with prompt version + judge score; drift report generated |
212	| **PR7** | Quantization + caching + context compression | `extraction/benchmark.py` (extend), caches in `retrieval/` | Quantized-vs-fp F1/latency/cost table; measured token reduction with held quality |
213	
214	Suggested order if time-boxed: PR1→PR2→PR3→PR4 first (the RAG + migration story carries
215	the most weight), then PR5→PR6 (LLMOps), then PR7 (cost/latency polish).
216	
217	---
218	
219	## 5. Free / OSS stack
220	
221	| Concern | Choice | Cost |
222	|---|---|---|
223	| Embeddings | BGE-M3 (`BAAI/bge-m3`) via sentence-transformers | free / local |
224	| Reranker | `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` | free / local |
225	| Vector DB | Qdrant (Docker, local) | free |
226	| LLM (live turn) | existing Gemini 2.5 Flash (already wired) | existing |
227	| LLM-as-judge | OSS model via Ollama/vLLM, or Gemini Flash | free / minimal |
228	| Logging store | SQLite + Parquet | free |
229	| CI | GitHub Actions | free tier |
230	| Corpus | public German policy/regulation text + synthetic claims; or your own mock CRM data | free |
231	
232	The paid voice/telephony pieces (Gradium, Twilio, LiveKit) are **untouched** — already
233	built. All new work runs offline against `scripts/run_demo_text.py`.
234	
235	---
236	
237	## 6. ZIH HPC usage (only where it earns its keep)
238	
239	ZIH (TU Dresden) GPU partitions via SLURM are the right tool for exactly two jobs;
240	everything else stays on your laptop.
241	
242	1. **Corpus embedding / backfill** (`slurm/embed_corpus.sbatch`): batch-embed the full
243	   corpus (and the `emb_v2` backfill in PR4) on a GPU. Makes the migration demo realistic
244	   (tens/hundreds of thousands of chunks) instead of toy-scale, and gives you a genuine
245	   "ran distributed batch jobs on an HPC SLURM scheduler" line.
246	2. **GLiNER2 fine-tune + quantize** (`slurm/finetune_quantize_gliner.sbatch`): re-fine-tune
247	   the extractor on more claim data and export an int8/ONNX serving artifact (PR7). A
248	   full fine-tune won't fit free Colab; an A100/H100 partition is the legitimate reason
249	   to use the cluster.
250	
251	Both scripts are templates — set your account/partition/module names. Keep them in the
252	repo: reviewers like seeing a real `sbatch` file.
253	
254	---
255	
256	## 7. Interview-question → where it's answered
257	
258	| Question (from your list) | Built in |
259	|---|---|
260	| Tokenization, embeddings, attention | embedder.py + README design notes; embeddings story in §3.3 |
261	| Fine-tuning, LoRA/QLoRA, layer freezing | GLiNER2 fine-tune (existing) + `slurm/finetune_quantize_gliner.sbatch` |
262	| Few-shot vs zero-shot, robust system prompts, determinism | prompt_registry + constrained extraction (§3.7, §3.9) |
263	| Track/version/backfill changing context; build memory | prompt_registry + Known-Context + migration (§3.4) |
264	| Chunking strategy | chunker.py (§3.1) |
265	| Choosing a vector DB | index.py + §3.2 |
266	| Zero-downtime embedding update/backfill | migrate.py (§3.4) — **the centerpiece** |
267	| Retrieval quality: precision@k, reranking, citation | eval.py + rerank.py (§3.5–3.6) |
268	| Pipeline raw→model→serving→feedback | full architecture (§2) |
269	| Monitor drift / hallucinations | drift_monitor.py + judge.py (§3.7) |
270	| Log prompts/outputs for debugging & auditing | logging_middleware.py (§3.7) |
271	| CI/CD for LLMs — what's different | eval_gate.py + workflow (§3.7) |
272	| Reduce token usage; quantize; batching+caching | §3.8 + PR7 |
273	| Hosted APIs vs OSS | §3.8 |
274	| More deterministic / less brittle; fallback mid-task | §3.9 |
275	| Solve without an LLM/vector DB; right DB | §3.2 + DataWhisper contrast |
276	| #7.1 embedding model changes — migrate safely | migrate.py (§3.4) |
277	| #7.2 fine-tune on behaviour & deploy | GLiNER2 fine-tune + serving (PR7) |
278	| #7.3 cheaper without killing quality | §3.8 caching/compression/quantization |
279	| #7.4 debug incorrect LLM outputs | logging traces + judge + eval (§3.7) |
280	
281	That's essentially the whole list from one repo.
282	
283	---
284	
285	## 8. Resume bullets (STAR, German-market tuned — claim only what you build)
286	
287	Use these once the corresponding PRs are merged; don't claim ahead of the code.
288	
289	- *Built a retrieval-grounded layer for a German-language claims-intake voice agent
290	  (Qdrant + BGE-M3 multilingual embeddings + cross-encoder reranking), so the agent
291	  cites the exact policy clause instead of generating coverage answers — measured at
292	  precision@k = X and groundedness = Y on a held-out evaluation set.*
293	- *Designed and shipped a **zero-downtime embedding-model migration** (named-vector
294	  dual-write, GPU backfill on the TU Dresden HPC cluster, shadow evaluation, atomic
295	  cutover with instant rollback) — re-indexed N chunks with no read downtime.*
296	- *Added an LLMOps spine: versioned prompt registry, an LLM-as-judge groundedness gate
297	  enforced in CI (blocks merges that regress retrieval/extraction metrics), and
298	  PII-redacted prompt/response audit logging with drift monitoring.*
299	- *Cut serving cost/latency by quantizing the entity extractor (int8/ONNX) and adding
300	  retrieval/embedding caching and context compression, holding extraction F1 within
301	  tolerance.*
302	
303	---
304	
305	## 9. Integration points in the existing repo (for whoever wires it)
306	
307	- `tools/` already exposes Tavily as a Gemini function-call → add `coverage_lookup` the
308	  same way (`retrieval/tool.py` provides the schema + handler).
309	- `agent/` (GeminiBrain) → load the system prompt from `llmops/prompt_registry.py`
310	  instead of a hard-coded string; wrap the model call with `llmops/logging_middleware.py`.
311	- `agent/pii_redact.py` → reuse as the redactor inside the logging middleware.

313	- `tests/juror_bot.py` → becomes one source of eval cases feeding `eval_gate.py`.
314	
315	---

317	## 10. De-hackathoning
318	
319	Replace the repo `README.md` with the one in this package, then apply
320	`DEHACKATHON_CHECKLIST.md` to the remaining docs (the ones not in this package).
321	Short version: remove hackathon/bounty/pitch framing, the "verified facts (April 2026) /

- Primary split on document structure (headings / § markers / numbered clauses).
- Secondary split only when a clause exceeds a max-token budget, with overlap.
- Each chunk keeps metadata: `doc_id, section_path, clause_id, doc_type, product_code, lang`.
- This metadata is the payload Qdrant filters on (e.g. restrict to the caller's tariff).

*Answers:* "What's your chunking strategy — length, semantics, or structure?"

### 3.2 Vector DB — Qdrant
Chosen over Chroma (great for prototypes, weaker filtering/ops) and pgvector (fine if
you're already on Postgres, weaker ANN ergonomics at scale). Qdrant gives:
- **Payload filtering** (tariff/product/lang) co-indexed with vectors — essential here.
- **Named vectors** in one collection → two embedding versions side by side, which is
  what makes the zero-downtime migration clean.
- Runs free locally in Docker; same API self-hosted on a server later.

*Answers:* "How do you choose a vector DB?" and "What's the right database for this task?"
(Note the contrast with `DataWhisper-AI`, which deliberately uses **no** vector DB —
NL→MongoDB structured queries. Keep that as the "when NOT to use vectors" example.)

### 3.3 Embeddings — multilingual, version-stamped
**BGE-M3** (multilingual, strong on German; dense + sparse + ColBERT-style multi-vector
if wanted). The corpus and callers are German; an English-only model would tank recall.
Every vector is written with the embedding **model id + dimension** recorded on the
collection/version, so nothing is ambiguous when a second model appears.

*Answers:* "How do embeddings work?" and feeds the migration story below.

### 3.4 Zero-downtime embedding migration — the centerpiece
The scenario: *"Your embedding model changes — how do you migrate safely?"* Plan:
1. **Versioned by construction.** Vectors live under a named vector (`emb_v1`). The
   pipeline records `embedding_version` in payload and on a small `index_meta` record.
2. **Dual-write.** When `emb_v2` is introduced, new ingests write *both* `emb_v1` and
   `emb_v2`. Reads still serve `emb_v1`.
3. **Backfill.** A batch job re-embeds the existing corpus into `emb_v2` (this is the
   **ZIH GPU job** — see §6). Idempotent, resumable, checkpointed.
4. **Shadow eval.** Run `retrieval/eval.py` against both `emb_v1` and `emb_v2` on the
   golden set. Only proceed if `emb_v2` is non-inferior (within tolerance) or better on
   precision@k / nDCG.
5. **Atomic cutover.** Flip the active version (alias / config flag) so reads serve
   `emb_v2`. No downtime — both vectors were already present.
6. **Rollback.** Flip back instantly; `emb_v1` is still there until you GC it.

*Answers:* "Can you update/backfill embeddings with zero downtime?" and Real-World
Scenario #1 end to end.

### 3.5 Reranking + citation
Bi-encoder recall (top-50) → **bge-reranker-v2-m3** cross-encoder → top-k. Every
returned chunk carries `section_path / clause_id`, so the agent answer cites the exact
clause ("covered under §4(2) of KK-300"). Groundedness is then *checkable*, which the
LLM-judge does.

*Answers:* reranking, citation, and the hallucination-monitoring story.

### 3.6 Retrieval evaluation
`retrieval/eval.py` computes **precision@k, recall@k, MRR, nDCG@k** against a golden
set of `query → relevant clause_ids`. The golden set is bootstrapped by generating
question/answer pairs *from* the corpus clauses (synthetic, then spot-checked), which is
free and reproducible.

*Answers:* "How do you evaluate retrieval quality?"

### 3.7 LLMOps — what actually differs from classic MLOps
- **Prompt registry:** every prompt is a versioned artifact (semver + content hash).
  The running agent loads `jamie_system@<version>`; logs record which version produced
  each response. No more "we changed the prompt and quality moved, no idea when."
- **CI eval gate (`.github/workflows/llm-eval.yml`):** on any change to prompts, model
  config, or retrieval, CI runs the eval suite and **fails the merge** if precision@k,
  groundedness, or extraction F1 drop beyond a threshold. *This is the key CI/CD-for-LLM
  difference:* you gate on **probabilistic eval metrics and an LLM-judge**, not on
  deterministic unit assertions. Tests are non-flaky-by-design via fixed seeds, a frozen
  eval set, and tolerance bands rather than exact-match.
- **Logging middleware:** wraps the Gemini call; persists `{trace_id, prompt_version,
  retrieved_ids, response, judge_scores, latency, token_counts}` — PII-redacted via the
  existing `agent/pii_redact.py` — to SQLite/Parquet for audit and debugging. In a
  regulated insurance context this is a feature, not overhead.
- **Drift + hallucination monitor:** rolling windows over groundedness rate, retrieval
  score distribution, and extraction F1; flags drift (e.g. groundedness < 0.9 sustained).

*Answers:* the whole MLOps/LLMOps cluster + "log prompts/outputs for debugging and
auditing" + "monitor performance drift or hallucinations" + the debugging-session
scenario (#7.4 — you now have the traces to do it).

### 3.8 Cost & latency
- **Quantize GLiNER2** (ONNX + int8 dynamic quantization) for serving; `extraction/
  benchmark.py` already produces F1/latency/cost — extend it to include the quantized
  variant. *Answers:* "when should you quantize?"
- **Caching:** embedding cache (content hash → vector), retrieval cache (query hash →
  results), and an optional semantic response cache. *Answers:* batching + caching.
- **Context compression:** rerank then keep top-k and trim each chunk to the relevant
  span before it enters the prompt → fewer tokens. *Answers:* "reduce token usage" and
  "cheaper without killing quality" (#7.3).
- **Hosted vs OSS:** Gemini Flash for the live conversational turn (latency + quality);
  OSS local models (embedder, reranker, GLiNER2) for everything offline/high-volume.
  *Answers:* "when to use hosted APIs vs open-source models?"

### 3.9 Determinism & fallback
- Structured outputs (the 15 pillars / 5 fraud signals) use constrained extraction
  (GLiNER2) rather than free-form generation → deterministic where it must be.
- The existing model fallback chain extends to a **retrieval fallback**: if Qdrant is
  unavailable or returns low-confidence, fall back to Tavily, then to a "I'll note that
  and a specialist will confirm" safe response — never hallucinate coverage.
*Answers:* "make the system more deterministic and less brittle" + "fallback if the LLM
fails mid-task".

---

## 4. PR-by-PR roadmap

Each PR is independently mergeable and demoable. Acceptance criteria are the interview
talking points.

| PR | Scope | Key files | Acceptance criteria |
|----|-------|-----------|---------------------|
| **PR1** | Corpus + structure-aware ingest + Qdrant index | `retrieval/{config,chunker,embedder,index}.py` | Corpus ingested; `index_meta` records embedding version; chunks carry section/clause metadata |
| **PR2** | Retriever + reranker + `coverage_lookup` tool wired into agent | `retrieval/{retriever,rerank,tool}.py`, `agent/` glue | Jamie can answer a coverage question with a cited clause in the text-mode demo |
| **PR3** | Retrieval eval + golden set | `retrieval/eval.py`, `spine/eval/golden_set.jsonl` | `precision@k / recall@k / MRR / nDCG` printed; numbers reproducible with a fixed seed |
| **PR4** | Zero-downtime migration | `retrieval/migrate.py` | Introduce `emb_v2`, dual-write, backfill, shadow-eval, atomic swap, rollback — all demoable, no read downtime |
| **PR5** | Prompt registry + CI eval gate | `llmops/{prompt_registry,judge,eval_gate}.py`, `.github/workflows/llm-eval.yml` | Prompt changes run CI eval; a deliberately worse prompt **fails** the gate |
| **PR6** | Logging middleware + drift monitor | `llmops/{logging_middleware,drift_monitor}.py` | Every turn logged (PII-redacted) with prompt version + judge score; drift report generated |
| **PR7** | Quantization + caching + context compression | `extraction/benchmark.py` (extend), caches in `retrieval/` | Quantized-vs-fp F1/latency/cost table; measured token reduction with held quality |

Suggested order if time-boxed: PR1→PR2→PR3→PR4 first (the RAG + migration story carries
the most weight), then PR5→PR6 (LLMOps), then PR7 (cost/latency polish).

The paid voice/telephony pieces (Gradium, Twilio, LiveKit) are **untouched** — already

## 6. ZIH HPC usage (only where it earns its keep)

ZIH (TU Dresden) GPU partitions via SLURM are the right tool for exactly two jobs;
everything else stays on your laptop.

1. **Corpus embedding / backfill** (`slurm/embed_corpus.sbatch`): batch-embed the full

Both scripts are templates — set your account/partition/module names. Keep them in the

content.text:
I've read the actual package — [BUILD_PLAN.md](echoclaim-spine/BUILD_PLAN.md), [DEHACKATHON_CHECKLIST.md](echoclaim-spine/DEHACKATHON_CHECKLIST.md), and the repo layout. Before I start wiring anything, I want to split this into the two very different things it actually contains, because I'll approach them differently.

## The part I'm glad to build (and it's the bulk of the value)

PR1→PR4 — structure-aware chunker, versioned embedder, Qdrant named-vector index, retriever + reranker, the `coverage_lookup` tool, retrieval eval (precision@k / nDCG), and the zero-downtime migration (`migrate.py`) — is real, senior-level engineering. Wiring it into the existing agent (`tools/`, `agent/` GeminiBrain, `pii_redact.py`) is a legitimate, high-value task. I'll happily build this with you, for real, in-repo. Same for the LLMOps spine (PR5→PR6).

Stripping genuine hackathon *marketing* cruft is also fine — prize/bounty amounts, codenames ("Operation: Turing Adjuster"), pitch lines, the H0–H24 race timeline. A portfolio project shouldn't carry that, and removing it isn't deception.

## The part I won't help frame the way the checklist frames it

The [DEHACKATHON_CHECKLIST.md](echoclaim-spine/DEHACKATHON_CHECKLIST.md) states its goal as removing "the tells that make docs look **AI-generated**" — deleting the AI build-journal, making "commit messages going forward boring and descriptive" to establish a non-hackathon style, a "de-AI" tone pass. Combined with the STAR resume bullets and the interview-question→code map, the *stated purpose* there is to make an interviewer believe this was hand-built senior work and conceal that it was AI-generated. I'm not going to help manufacture that false provenance — laundering commit history to disguise authorship, or resume bullets that claim work you didn't actually do.

Here's the thing though: **your own doc already has the right principle in it** — §8 says *"claim only what you build"* and *"don't claim ahead of the code."* Run with that and the whole problem dissolves. If you genuinely build PR1→PR4, understand it, and can whiteboard *why named vectors enable a clean cutover* or *what makes the backfill idempotent*, then it **is** your work — using me as a tool to build it doesn't change that, and you have nothing to hide. That's also the only version that survives a real interview: a good interviewer will probe ("walk me through what breaks if the dual-write fails halfway"), and laundered provenance collapses there while real understanding doesn't.

So my proposal: let's actually build it. You own it because you built it and can defend it — not because we scrubbed the fingerprints.

Want me to start on **PR1** (corpus + structure-aware ingest + Qdrant index: `retrieval/{config,chunker,embedder,index}.py`)? I'll wire it against the existing repo and we go module by module so you understand each piece well enough to defend it. Or if you'd rather, I can start with the migration design (PR4) since that's the centerpiece.

"""Central configuration for the retrieval subsystem.

Everything that two modules must agree on (model ids, vector names, dimensions,
collection names, top-k) lives here so nothing drifts out of sync.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EmbeddingVersion:
    """A named, versioned embedding configuration.

    The `name` is the Qdrant *named vector* key, so two versions coexist in one
    collection — this is what makes the zero-downtime migration clean.
    """
    name: str          # qdrant named-vector key, e.g. "emb_v1"
    model_id: str      # huggingface id, e.g. "BAAI/bge-m3"
    dim: int           # vector dimension


# Registered embedding versions. Add a new entry to introduce a model; never edit
# an existing one in place (that would invalidate vectors already written under it).
EMBEDDING_VERSIONS: dict[str, EmbeddingVersion] = {
    "emb_v1": EmbeddingVersion("emb_v1", "BAAI/bge-m3", 1024),
    # "emb_v2": EmbeddingVersion("emb_v2", "<next-model>", <dim>),  # added in PR4
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    qdrant_url: str = os.getenv("QDRANT_URL", "http://localhost:6333")
    qdrant_api_key: str | None = os.getenv("QDRANT_API_KEY")
    collection: str = os.getenv("QDRANT_COLLECTION", "echoclaim_policies")

    # The version reads are served from. Migration flips this (see migrate.py).
    active_version: str = os.getenv("ACTIVE_EMBED_VERSION", "emb_v1")
    # When set, ingests also write this version's vectors (dual-write phase).
    dual_write_version: str | None = os.getenv("DUAL_WRITE_EMBED_VERSION") or None

    rerank_model_id: str = os.getenv("RERANK_MODEL_ID", "BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3")

    # Structure-aware chunking budget (see chunker.py).
    max_chunk_tokens: int = int(os.getenv("MAX_CHUNK_TOKENS", "400"))
    chunk_overlap_tokens: int = int(os.getenv("CHUNK_OVERLAP_TOKENS", "64"))

    top_k_recall: int = int(os.getenv("TOP_K_RECALL", "50"))   # bi-encoder candidates
    top_k_final: int = int(os.getenv("TOP_K_FINAL", "6"))      # after rerank

    embed_batch_size: int = int(os.getenv("EMBED_BATCH_SIZE", "64"))
    embed_cache_path: str = os.getenv("EMBED_CACHE_PATH", ".cache/embeddings.sqlite")

    versions: dict[str, EmbeddingVersion] = field(default_factory=lambda: EMBEDDING_VERSIONS)

    def version(self, name: str) -> EmbeddingVersion:
        return self.versions[name]


settings = Settings()

"""Structure-aware chunking for policy / regulatory documents.

Policies are hierarchical (Teil -> § -> Absatz -> Satz). Fixed-length windows shred
a clause across chunk boundaries and wreck retrievability, so we split on structure
first and only fall back to token windows when a single clause is too large.

See BUILD_PLAN.md section 3.1.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Chunk:
    text: str
    doc_id: str
    section_path: str           # e.g. "Teil B / §4 / Abs. 2"
    clause_id: str              # stable id for citation, e.g. "KK-300:§4(2)"
    doc_type: str               # "policy" | "regulation" | "claim" | "faq"
    product_code: str | None    # tariff/product filter key, e.g. "KK-300"
    lang: str = "de"
    token_count: int = 0
    id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))

    def payload(self) -> dict:
        """Qdrant payload — also the citation source and the filter keys."""
        return {
            "doc_id": self.doc_id,
            "section_path": self.section_path,
            "clause_id": self.clause_id,
            "doc_type": self.doc_type,
            "product_code": self.product_code,
            "lang": self.lang,
            "text": self.text,
        }


# Matches German clause markers like "§ 4", "Abs. 2", numbered headings, etc.
_SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^(?:\s*)(§\s*\d+[a-z]?|Teil\s+[A-Z0-9]+|\d+(?:\.\d+)*\s+\S)")


def estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    """Cheap token estimate (~4 chars/token). Swap for a real tokenizer if needed."""
    return max(1, len(text) // 4)


def split_on_structure(raw: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Return [(section_marker, body)] by splitting on structural markers.

    TODO: replace the regex with a real layout/heading parser for PDFs
    (the corpus loader in ingest can hand us already-segmented sections).
    """
    matches = list(_SECTION_RE.finditer(raw))
    if not matches:
        return [("", raw.strip())]
    spans: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for i, m in enumerate(matches):
        start = m.start()
        end = matches[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(matches) else len(raw)
        marker = m.group(1).strip()
        spans.append((marker, raw[start:end].strip()))
    return spans


def _window(text: str, max_tokens: int, overlap: int) -> list[str]:
    """Secondary split: sliding token windows with overlap, for oversized clauses."""
    words = text.split()
    if estimate_tokens(text) <= max_tokens:
        return [text]
    approx_words = max_tokens * 4 // 1  # rough words-per-window from char/token ratio
    step = max(1, approx_words - overlap)
    out = []
    for i in range(0, len(words), step):
        out.append(" ".join(words[i:i + approx_words]))
        if i + approx_words >= len(words):
            break
    return out


def chunk_document(
    raw: str,
    *,
    doc_id: str,
    doc_type: str,
    product_code: str | None,
    lang: str = "de",
    max_tokens: int = 400,
    overlap: int = 64,
) -> list[Chunk]:
    """Structure-first, token-window-second chunking."""
    chunks: list[Chunk] = []
    for marker, body in split_on_structure(raw):
        section_path = marker or "root"
        for j, piece in enumerate(_window(body, max_tokens, overlap)):
            clause_id = f"{product_code or doc_id}:{marker or 'root'}"
            if j > 0:
                clause_id += f"#{j}"
            chunks.append(
                Chunk(
                    text=piece,
                    doc_id=doc_id,
                    section_path=section_path,
                    clause_id=clause_id,
                    doc_type=doc_type,
                    product_code=product_code,
                    lang=lang,
                    token_count=estimate_tokens(piece),
                )
            )
    return chunks

1	"""Versioned embedding wrapper.
2	
3	Each Embedder is bound to one EmbeddingVersion, so the model id and dimension travel
4	with every vector it produces. Includes a content-hash cache so re-ingest and the
5	migration backfill never re-embed unchanged text.
6	
7	See BUILD_PLAN.md sections 3.3 and 3.4.
8	"""
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import hashlib
12	import sqlite3
13	from pathlib import Path
14	
15	import numpy as np
16	
17	from .config import EmbeddingVersion, settings
18	
19	
20	def content_hash(text: str, model_id: str) -> str:
21	    return hashlib.sha256(f"{model_id}\x00{text}".encode()).hexdigest()
22	
23	
24	class _SqliteVectorCache:
25	    """Tiny persistent cache: (hash) -> float32 vector bytes."""
26	
27	    def __init__(self, path: str):
28	        Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
29	        self.con = sqlite3.connect(path)
30	        self.con.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vec (h TEXT PRIMARY KEY, v BLOB)")
31	
32	    def get(self, h: str) -> np.ndarray | None:
33	        row = self.con.execute("SELECT v FROM vec WHERE h=?", (h,)).fetchone()
34	        return np.frombuffer(row[0], dtype=np.float32) if row else None
35	
36	    def put(self, h: str, v: np.ndarray) -> None:
37	        self.con.execute(
38	            "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO vec VALUES (?, ?)", (h, v.astype(np.float32).tobytes())
39	        )
40	        self.con.commit()
41	
42	
43	class Embedder:
44	    def __init__(self, version: EmbeddingVersion, use_cache: bool = True):
45	        self.version = version
46	        self._cache = _SqliteVectorCache(settings.embed_cache_path) if use_cache else None
47	        self._model = None  # lazy
48	
49	    def _load(self):
50	        if self._model is None:
51	            # Imported lazily so the module is importable without the heavy dep.
52	            from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
53	
54	            self._model = SentenceTransformer(self.version.model_id)
55	        return self._model
56	
57	    def encode(self, texts: list[str]) -> np.ndarray:
58	        """Return (len(texts), dim) float32, normalized for cosine."""
59	        out: list[np.ndarray | None] = [None] * len(texts)
60	        todo_idx, todo_txt = [], []
61	        for i, t in enumerate(texts):
62	            cached = self._cache.get(content_hash(t, self.version.model_id)) if self._cache else None
63	            if cached is not None:
64	                out[i] = cached
65	            else:
66	                todo_idx.append(i)
67	                todo_txt.append(t)
68	
69	        if todo_txt:
70	            model = self._load()

4	Reads target the active version; the migration writes a second version alongside the
5	first and flips the active pointer atomically. See BUILD_PLAN.md sections 3.2 and 3.4.
6	"""

8	
9	from dataclasses import dataclass
10	
11	from .chunker import Chunk
12	from .config import settings
13	
14	
15	@dataclass
16	class Hit:
17	    score: float
18	    payload: dict
19	
20	    @property
21	    def clause_id(self) -> str:
22	        return self.payload.get("clause_id", "")
23

25	    def text(self) -> str:

27	
28	
29	class QdrantIndex:
30	    def __init__(self):
31	        from qdrant_client import QdrantClient
32	
33	        self.client = QdrantClient(url=settings.qdrant_url, api_key=settings.qdrant_api_key)
34	        self.collection = settings.collection
35	
36	    # ---- schema / versions ---------------------------------------------------
37	
38	    def ensure_collection(self, version_names: list[str]) -> None:
39	        """Create the collection (if absent) with one named vector per version."""
40	        from qdrant_client import models
41	
42	        vectors_config = {
43	            name: models.VectorParams(
44	                size=settings.version(name).dim, distance=models.Distance.COSINE
45	            )
46	            for name in version_names
47	        }
48	        existing = {c.name for c in self.client.get_collections().collections}
49	        if self.collection not in existing:
50	            self.client.create_collection(self.collection, vectors_config=vectors_config)
51	            self._set_meta({"versions": version_names, "active": settings.active_version})
52	        else:
53	            self.add_vector_version(version_names)
54	
55	    def add_vector_version(self, version_names: list[str]) -> None:
56	        """Add a new named vector to an existing collection (PR4, dual-write setup).
57	
58	        NOTE: adding a named vector in place requires a recent Qdrant. If the running
59	        server is too old, create `{collection}__v2`, backfill, then swap by alias.
60	        """
61	        from qdrant_client import models
62	
63	        meta = self._get_meta()
64	        known = set(meta.get("versions", []))
65	        new = [v for v in version_names if v not in known]
66	        for name in new:
67	            # TODO: confirm server version supports update_collection vector add;
68	            # otherwise fall back to the side-collection + alias strategy noted above.
69	            self.client.update_collection(
70	                self.collection,
71	                vectors_config={
72	                    name: models.VectorParams(
73	                        size=settings.version(name).dim, distance=models.Distance.COSINE
74	                    )
75	                },
76	            )
77	        if new:
78	            meta["versions"] = sorted(known | set(new))
79	            self._set_meta(meta)

84	        """Upsert points carrying one or more named vectors.
85

87	        Dual-write = pass two versions here.
88	        """
89	        from qdrant_client import models
90	
91	        points = []
92	        for i, ch in enumerate(chunks):
93	            vector = {v: vectors_by_version[v][i].tolist() for v in vectors_by_version}
94	            points.append(models.PointStruct(id=ch.id, vector=vector, payload=ch.payload()))
95	        self.client.upsert(self.collection, points=points, wait=True)

"""Smoke tests — fast, no network, no API keys.

These prove the modules import + the core data path works.
Run with:  pytest -q
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


def test_crm_profiles_load():
    for name in ["max_mueller", "helga_schmidt", "thomas_weber_fleet"]:
        p = REPO / "data" / "crm" / f"{name}.json"
        data = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        assert data["policyholder"]["name"]
        assert data["policy"]["policy_number"]


def test_pii_redact():
    from agent.pii_redact import redact
    sample = "policy DE-HUK-2024-884421 plate B-MM 4421 vin WVWZZZ1JZ3W386752"
    out = redact(sample)
    assert "884421" not in out
    assert "[POLICY]" in out
    assert "[PLATE]" in out
    assert "[VIN]" in out


def test_pii_redact_extended():
    """Aikido-bounty patterns: credit card, social security, health card,
    multi-segment phone, IBAN, DOB, email — none of these should leak even
    when they appear in a single transcript line."""
    from agent.pii_redact import redact

    # Credit card with separators
    out = redact("My card 4242 4242 4242 4242.")
    assert "4242" not in out, f"credit card leaked: {out!r}"
    assert "[CARD]" in out

    # Credit card without separators
    out = redact("Card no 4111111111111111 expires.")
    assert "4111111111111111" not in out
    assert "[CARD]" in out

    # IBAN
    out = redact("DE89 3704 0044 0532 0130 00 is mine.")
    assert "3704" not in out
    assert "[IBAN]" in out

    # German Sozialversicherungsnummer
    out = redact("SVNR 12 030484 W 023 handed over.")
    assert "030484" not in out
    assert "[SVNR]" in out

    # Multi-segment phone
    out = redact("Phone +49 172 555 0100 anytime.")
    # The full digit sequence shouldn't survive — at minimum the last group
    # (which the older regex was missing) must be redacted.
    assert "0100" not in out, f"phone tail leaked: {out!r}"
    assert "[PHONE]" in out

    # Email
    out = redact("Send to max.mueller@email.de please.")
    assert "max.mueller" not in out
    assert "[EMAIL]" in out

    # DOB ISO format
    out = redact("DOB 1984-03-15 confirmed.")
    assert "1984" not in out
    assert "[DOB]" in out

"""PII redaction for logs / persisted transcripts.

Insurance calls are full of GDPR Article 9 (health) and Article 6 (financial)
data.  This module is the audit-friendly answer to "you handle sensitive data,
how do you log it?" — and the load-bearing piece of the Aikido bounty pitch.

Use `redact(text)` on anything before it touches a log handler or disk.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

# Roughly: "DE-" then 3 letters, "-2024-", 6 digits  (and similar carrier codes)
POLICY_NUMBER = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z]{2}-[A-Z]{2,4}-\d{4}-\d{4,8}\b")

# German plate: 1–3 letters, "-", 1–2 letters, 1–4 digits
PLATE = re.compile(r"\b[A-ZÄÖÜ]{1,3}-[A-Z]{1,2}\s?\d{1,4}\b")

# 17-character VIN
VIN = re.compile(r"\b[A-HJ-NPR-Z0-9]{17}\b")

# German phone — supports 2/3/4 digit groups, country prefix optional.
# Catches "+49 172 555 0100", "+49-172-555-0100", "0172 5550100", etc.
PHONE = re.compile(
    r"\+?\d{1,3}[\s\-]?\d{2,5}[\s\-]?\d{2,4}(?:[\s\-]?\d{2,5})?"
)

# IBAN (DE only is fine for our use)
IBAN = re.compile(r"\bDE\d{2}[\s\-]?(?:\d{4}[\s\-]?){4}\d{2}\b")

# DOB-ish: yyyy-mm-dd
DOB = re.compile(r"\b(?:19|20)\d{2}-\d{2}-\d{2}\b")

# Email
EMAIL = re.compile(r"\b[\w.\-]+@[\w.\-]+\.\w{2,}\b")

# Credit card — 13–19 digit groups separated by spaces or hyphens.  Validated
# loosely (we don't run Luhn) — better to over-redact a similar-shaped number
# than leak a real card.
CREDIT_CARD = re.compile(r"\b(?:\d[ \-]?){13,19}\b")

# German Sozialversicherungsnummer (social security): 12 chars,
# 2 digits + 1 letter + 7 digits + 2 letters.  e.g. "12 030484 W 023".
SOCIAL_SECURITY_DE = re.compile(
    r"\b\d{2}\s?\d{6}\s?[A-Z]\s?\d{3}\b"
)

# German health insurance card number (Krankenversichertennummer):
# 1 letter + 9 digits, sometimes with a check digit (10 total).
HEALTH_CARD_DE = re.compile(r"\b[A-Z]\d{9,10}\b")

# German driver's license number — alphanumeric ~11 chars.  Format varies
# by Bundesland but typically: letter or digit blocks.  Conservative: catch
# any 10–12 char alphanumeric with at least one letter and at least one digit.
DRIVER_LICENSE_DE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?=[A-Z0-9]{10,12}\b)(?=[A-Z0-9]*[A-Z])(?=[A-Z0-9]*\d)[A-Z0-9]{10,12}\b"
)

# Generic credit-card-like Luhn-eligible 16-digit run (catches stripped formats).
CC_NO_SEPARATORS = re.compile(r"\b\d{16}\b")

PATTERNS: list[tuple[re.Pattern[str], str]] = [
    # Order matters — apply MOST SPECIFIC patterns first so the looser
    # ones (PHONE, CREDIT_CARD) don't greedily consume well-formatted IDs
    # before they're recognised.  E.g. PHONE alone would otherwise eat
    # an ISO date like "1984-03-15" because it parses as 4-digit + 2-digit
    # + 2-digit groups.
    (DOB, "[DOB]"),
    (POLICY_NUMBER, "[POLICY]"),
    (VIN, "[VIN]"),
    (IBAN, "[IBAN]"),
    (SOCIAL_SECURITY_DE, "[SVNR]"),
    (HEALTH_CARD_DE, "[HEALTH_CARD]"),
    (DRIVER_LICENSE_DE, "[DL]"),
    (CREDIT_CARD, "[CARD]"),
    (CC_NO_SEPARATORS, "[CARD]"),
    (PLATE, "[PLATE]"),
    (EMAIL, "[EMAIL]"),
    (PHONE, "[PHONE]"),
]


def redact(text: str) -> str:
    """Return *text* with all PII patterns replaced by tokens."""
    for pat, tok in PATTERNS:
        text = pat.sub(tok, text)
    return text


def redacted_dict(d: dict) -> dict:
    """Recursively redact string values in a dict.  Keys are preserved."""
    out: dict = {}
    for k, v in d.items():
        if isinstance(v, str):
            out[k] = redact(v)
        elif isinstance(v, dict):
            out[k] = redacted_dict(v)
        elif isinstance(v, list):
            out[k] = [redact(x) if isinstance(x, str) else x for x in v]
        else:
            out[k] = v
    return out


# --- self-test -------------------------------------------------------------
if __name__ == "__main__":
    sample = (
        "My policy is DE-HUK-2024-884421, VIN WVWZZZ1JZ3W386752, plate B-MM 4421, "
        "phone +49 172 555 0100, email max.mueller@email.de, born 1984-03-15."
    )
    print(redact(sample))

"""Central configuration for the retrieval subsystem.

Everything two modules must agree on (model ids, vector names, dimensions, collection
names, top-k) lives here so nothing drifts out of sync. All values are env-overridable
so the same code runs against a local Docker Qdrant, a hosted cluster, or the offline
hash-embedder path used by tests and CI.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EmbeddingVersion:
    """A named, versioned embedding configuration.

    ``name`` is the Qdrant *named vector* key, so two versions can coexist in one
    collection — this is what makes the zero-downtime migration (PR4) clean.
    """
    name: str          # qdrant named-vector key, e.g. "emb_v1"
    model_id: str      # huggingface id, e.g. "BAAI/bge-m3"
    dim: int           # vector dimension


# Registered embedding versions. Add a new entry to introduce a model; never edit an
# existing one in place — that would invalidate vectors already written under it.
EMBEDDING_VERSIONS: dict[str, EmbeddingVersion] = {
    "emb_v1": EmbeddingVersion("emb_v1", "BAAI/bge-m3", 1024),
    # "emb_v2": EmbeddingVersion("emb_v2", "<next-model>", <dim>),  # added in PR4
}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    qdrant_url: str = os.getenv("QDRANT_URL", "http://localhost:6333")
    qdrant_api_key: str | None = os.getenv("QDRANT_API_KEY")
    collection: str = os.getenv("QDRANT_COLLECTION", "echoclaim_policies")

    # The version reads are served from. Migration flips this (see migrate.py, PR4).
    active_version: str = os.getenv("ACTIVE_EMBED_VERSION", "emb_v1")
    # When set, ingests also write this version's vectors (dual-write phase).
    dual_write_version: str | None = os.getenv("DUAL_WRITE_EMBED_VERSION") or None

    # Embedding backend. "sentence-transformers" loads the real BGE-M3 model;
    # "hash" is a deterministic, dependency-free embedder for offline tests, CI,
    # and reproducible migration shadow-evals. See embedder.get_embedder.
    embed_backend: str = os.getenv("EMBED_BACKEND", "sentence-transformers")

    rerank_model_id: str = os.getenv("RERANK_MODEL_ID", "BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3")

    # Structure-aware chunking budget (see chunker.py).
    max_chunk_tokens: int = int(os.getenv("MAX_CHUNK_TOKENS", "400"))
    chunk_overlap_tokens: int = int(os.getenv("CHUNK_OVERLAP_TOKENS", "64"))

    top_k_recall: int = int(os.getenv("TOP_K_RECALL", "50"))   # bi-encoder candidates
    top_k_final: int = int(os.getenv("TOP_K_FINAL", "6"))      # after rerank

    embed_batch_size: int = int(os.getenv("EMBED_BATCH_SIZE", "64"))

"""Structure-aware chunking for policy / regulatory documents.

German insurance policies are hierarchical (Teil -> § -> Absatz -> Satz). Fixed-length
windows shred a clause across chunk boundaries and wreck retrievability, so we split on
structure first and only fall back to token windows when a single clause exceeds the
token budget. Each chunk keeps the metadata that doubles as the citation source and the
Qdrant filter keys (product_code, lang, ...).

See echoclaim-spine/BUILD_PLAN.md section 3.1.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Chunk:
    text: str
    doc_id: str
    section_path: str           # e.g. "Teil B / §4 / Abs. 2"
    clause_id: str              # stable id for citation, e.g. "KK-300:§4(2)"
    doc_type: str               # "policy" | "regulation" | "claim" | "faq"
    product_code: str | None    # tariff/product filter key, e.g. "KK-300"
    lang: str = "de"
    token_count: int = 0
    id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))

    def payload(self) -> dict:
        """Qdrant payload — also the citation source and the filter keys."""
        return {
            "doc_id": self.doc_id,
            "section_path": self.section_path,
            "clause_id": self.clause_id,
            "doc_type": self.doc_type,
            "product_code": self.product_code,
            "lang": self.lang,
            "text": self.text,
        }


# Matches German clause markers like "§ 4", "Teil B", numbered headings "4.2 ...".
_SECTION_RE = re.compile(r"(?m)^(?:\s*)(§\s*\d+[a-z]?|Teil\s+[A-Z0-9]+|\d+(?:\.\d+)*\s+\S)")


def estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    """Cheap token estimate (~4 chars/token). Swap for a real tokenizer if needed."""
    return max(1, len(text) // 4)


def split_on_structure(raw: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    """Return [(section_marker, body)] by splitting on structural markers.

    The corpus loader hands us plain text; for PDFs a layout parser would feed
    already-segmented sections here instead of the regex.
    """
    matches = list(_SECTION_RE.finditer(raw))
    if not matches:
        return [("", raw.strip())]
    spans: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for i, m in enumerate(matches):
        start = m.start()
        end = matches[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(matches) else len(raw)
        marker = m.group(1).strip()
        spans.append((marker, raw[start:end].strip()))
    return spans


def _window(text: str, max_tokens: int, overlap: int) -> list[str]:
    """Secondary split: token-budgeted word windows with overlap, for oversized clauses.

    Word count per window is derived from *this* text's actual char/token density
    rather than a fixed guess, so a budget expressed in tokens maps to a sensible
    number of words regardless of how long the words are.
    """
    words = text.split()
    if estimate_tokens(text) <= max_tokens or not words:
        return [text]
    tok_per_word = max(1.0, estimate_tokens(text) / len(words))
    words_per_window = max(1, int(max_tokens / tok_per_word))
    overlap_words = min(words_per_window - 1, max(0, int(overlap / tok_per_word)))
    step = max(1, words_per_window - overlap_words)
    out: list[str] = []
    for i in range(0, len(words), step):
        out.append(" ".join(words[i:i + words_per_window]))
        if i + words_per_window >= len(words):
            break
    return out


def chunk_document(
    raw: str,
    *,
    doc_id: str,
    doc_type: str,
    product_code: str | None,
    lang: str = "de",
    max_tokens: int = 400,
    overlap: int = 64,
) -> list[Chunk]:
    """Structure-first, token-window-second chunking."""
    chunks: list[Chunk] = []
    for marker, body in split_on_structure(raw):
        if not body:
            continue
        section_path = marker or "root"
        for j, piece in enumerate(_window(body, max_tokens, overlap)):
            clause_id = f"{product_code or doc_id}:{marker or 'root'}"
            if j > 0:
                clause_id += f"#{j}"
            chunks.append(
                Chunk(
                    text=piece,
                    doc_id=doc_id,
                    section_path=section_path,
                    clause_id=clause_id,
                    doc_type=doc_type,
                    product_code=product_code,
                    lang=lang,
                    token_count=estimate_tokens(piece),
                )
            )
    return chunks

"""Corpus loader.

Reads the policy / tariff / regulation corpus from ``data/policies/*.md``. Each file
carries optional YAML front matter (delimited by ``---``) with the metadata that becomes
the chunk's citation + filter keys; the body is the clause text the chunker splits on.

    ---
    doc_id: kk-300
    doc_type: policy        # policy | regulation | claim | faq
    product_code: KK-300
    lang: de
    ---
    Teil A — ...
    § 1 ...
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

import yaml


@dataclass
class CorpusDoc:
    doc_id: str
    doc_type: str
    product_code: str | None
    lang: str
    text: str
    source_path: str


def _parse_front_matter(raw: str) -> tuple[dict, str]:
    if raw.startswith("---"):
        end = raw.find("\n---", 3)
        if end != -1:
            header = raw[3:end].strip()
            body = raw[end + 4:].lstrip("\n")
            return (yaml.safe_load(header) or {}), body
    return {}, raw


def load_doc(path: Path) -> CorpusDoc:
    meta, body = _parse_front_matter(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return CorpusDoc(
        doc_id=str(meta.get("doc_id") or path.stem),
        doc_type=str(meta.get("doc_type") or "policy"),
        product_code=(str(meta["product_code"]) if meta.get("product_code") else None),
        lang=str(meta.get("lang") or "de"),
        text=body.strip(),
        source_path=str(path),
    )


def load_corpus(corpus_dir: str | Path) -> list[CorpusDoc]:
    root = Path(corpus_dir)
    if not root.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"corpus dir not found: {root}")
    docs = [load_doc(p) for p in sorted(root.glob("*.md"))]
    if not docs:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no .md corpus files in {root}")
    return docs

"""Corpus ingest: load -> chunk -> embed -> upsert into the Qdrant named-vector index.

This is the PR1 entrypoint. It writes the active embedding version (plus the dual-write
version, if one is configured for a migration) and records an ``index_meta`` manifest so
the embedding version that produced each index is never ambiguous.

Run it::

    python -m retrieval.ingest                 # ingest into Qdrant
    python -m retrieval.ingest --dry-run       # chunk + embed + write manifest, no Qdrant
    EMBED_BACKEND=hash python -m retrieval.ingest --dry-run   # offline, no model download

If Qdrant is unreachable, ingest degrades to a dry run with a warning rather than
failing — matching the repo's "the demo never breaks" tool convention.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import time
from pathlib import Path

from .chunker import Chunk, chunk_document
from .config import settings
from .corpus import load_corpus
from .embedder import get_embedder


def load_and_chunk(corpus_dir: str | None = None) -> list[Chunk]:
    docs = load_corpus(corpus_dir or settings.corpus_dir)
    chunks: list[Chunk] = []
    for d in docs:
        chunks.extend(
            chunk_document(
                d.text,
                doc_id=d.doc_id,
                doc_type=d.doc_type,
                product_code=d.product_code,
                lang=d.lang,
                max_tokens=settings.max_chunk_tokens,
                overlap=settings.chunk_overlap_tokens,
            )
        )
    return chunks


def _target_versions() -> list[str]:
    """Active version, plus the dual-write version during a migration."""
    versions = [settings.active_version]
    if settings.dual_write_version and settings.dual_write_version not in versions:
        versions.append(settings.dual_write_version)
    return versions


def _write_manifest(manifest: dict) -> None:
    path = Path(settings.ingest_manifest_path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")


def ingest(corpus_dir: str | None = None, *, dry_run: bool = False, backend: str | None = None) -> dict:
    chunks = load_and_chunk(corpus_dir)
    versions = _target_versions()

    vectors_by_version = {}
    for name in versions:
        emb = get_embedder(settings.version(name), backend=backend)
        vectors_by_version[name] = emb.encode([c.text for c in chunks])

    manifest = {
        "collection": settings.collection,
        "active": settings.active_version,
        "versions": versions,
        "embedding_versions": {
            name: {"model_id": settings.version(name).model_id, "dim": settings.version(name).dim}
            for name in versions
        },
        "backend": backend or settings.embed_backend,
        "n_docs": len({c.doc_id for c in chunks}),
        "n_chunks": len(chunks),
        "created_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
        "dry_run": dry_run,
    }

    if not dry_run:
        try:
            from .index import QdrantIndex

            idx = QdrantIndex()
            idx.ensure_collection(versions)
            idx.upsert(chunks, vectors_by_version)
            manifest["upserted"] = True
        except Exception as exc:  # qdrant not running / client missing -> manifest-only
            print(f"[ingest] Qdrant unavailable ({exc}); writing manifest only.")
            manifest["dry_run"] = True
            manifest["upserted"] = False

    _write_manifest(manifest)
    return manifest


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Ingest the policy corpus into the retrieval index.")
    ap.add_argument("--corpus-dir", default=None, help="override CORPUS_DIR")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="chunk + embed + manifest, no Qdrant")
    ap.add_argument("--backend", default=None, help="embed backend override: sentence-transformers | hash")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    m = ingest(args.corpus_dir, dry_run=args.dry_run, backend=args.backend)
    print(json.dumps(m, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    print(
        f"\n[ingest] {m['n_chunks']} chunks from {m['n_docs']} docs "
        f"-> versions {m['versions']} (backend={m['backend']}); "
        f"manifest at {settings.ingest_manifest_path}"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        "n_chunks": len(chunks),
        "created_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
        "dry_run": dry_run,
    }

    if not dry_run:
        try:
            from .index import QdrantIndex

            idx = QdrantIndex()
            idx.ensure_collection(versions)
            idx.upsert(chunks, vectors_by_version)
            manifest["upserted"] = True
        except Exception as exc:  # qdrant not running / client missing -> manifest-only
            print(f"[ingest] Qdrant unavailable ({exc}); writing manifest only.")
            manifest["dry_run"] = True
            manifest["upserted"] = False

    _write_manifest(manifest)
    return manifest


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Ingest the policy corpus into the retrieval index.")
    ap.add_argument("--corpus-dir", default=None, help="override CORPUS_DIR")
    ap.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="chunk + embed + manifest, no Qdrant")
    ap.add_argument("--backend", default=None, help="embed backend override: sentence-transformers | hash")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    m = ingest(args.corpus_dir, dry_run=args.dry_run, backend=args.backend)
    print(json.dumps(m, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    print(
        f"\n[ingest] {m['n_chunks']} chunks from {m['n_docs']} docs "
        f"-> versions {m['versions']} (backend={m['backend']}); "
        f"manifest at {settings.ingest_manifest_path}"
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Retrieval PR1 tests — fast, offline, no Qdrant, no model download.

Proves the ingest data path: structure-aware chunking, corpus loading, the deterministic
hash embedder, and a dry-run ingest that records the embedding version. Run with:
    EMBED_BACKEND=hash pytest -q tests/test_retrieval.py
(the ingest test forces the hash backend explicitly, so the env var is optional).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from retrieval.chunker import chunk_document, estimate_tokens, split_on_structure
from retrieval.config import settings
from retrieval.corpus import load_corpus
from retrieval.embedder import get_embedder

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


# ---- chunker -------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_split_on_structure_keeps_paragraph_markers():
    raw = "§ 1 Erstes\nText eins.\n§ 2 Zweites\nText zwei."
    spans = split_on_structure(raw)
    markers = [m for m, _ in spans]
    assert "§ 1" in markers and "§ 2" in markers


def test_chunk_metadata_is_citation_ready():
    raw = "§ 4 Entwendung\n(1) Bei Entwendung ersetzt der Versicherer den Wert.\n"
    chunks = chunk_document(raw, doc_id="kk-300", doc_type="policy", product_code="KK-300")
    assert chunks
    c = chunks[0]
    assert c.clause_id.startswith("KK-300:§ 4")
    assert c.section_path == "§ 4"
    assert c.product_code == "KK-300"
    assert c.lang == "de"
    # payload carries exactly the keys the index filters + cites on
    assert {"clause_id", "section_path", "product_code", "lang", "text"} <= set(c.payload())


def test_oversized_clause_is_window_split_with_overlap():
    # One clause well over the budget must split into multiple chunks (no marker loss).
    body = "§ 9 Lang\n" + " ".join(f"wort{i}" for i in range(400))
    chunks = chunk_document(body, doc_id="d", doc_type="policy",
                            product_code=None, max_tokens=50, overlap=10)
    assert len(chunks) > 1, "oversized clause should split into multiple windows"
    assert all(c.token_count <= 80 for c in chunks), "windows should respect the token budget"
    # secondary splits get a #n suffix so each chunk has a distinct clause id
    assert any("#" in c.clause_id for c in chunks)


# ---- corpus --------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_corpus_loads_with_front_matter():
    docs = load_corpus(REPO / "data" / "policies")
    by_id = {d.doc_id: d for d in docs}
    assert "kk-300" in by_id and "vvg-auszug" in by_id
    assert by_id["kk-300"].product_code == "KK-300"
    assert by_id["kk-300"].doc_type == "policy"
    assert by_id["vvg-auszug"].doc_type == "regulation"
    assert by_id["vvg-auszug"].product_code is None
    assert "Entwendung" in by_id["kk-300"].text  # front matter stripped, body intact


# ---- embedder (hash backend) ---------------------------------------------------

def test_hash_embedder_is_deterministic_and_normalized():
    v1 = settings.version("emb_v1")
    emb = get_embedder(v1, backend="hash")
    a = emb.encode(["Stoßstangenschaden durch Parkrempler", "etwas anderes"])
    b = emb.encode(["Stoßstangenschaden durch Parkrempler", "etwas anderes"])
    assert a.shape == (2, v1.dim)
    assert np.allclose(a, b), "hash embedder must be reproducible"
    assert np.allclose(np.linalg.norm(a, axis=1), 1.0, atol=1e-5), "vectors must be L2-normalized"
    assert not np.allclose(a[0], a[1]), "distinct text -> distinct vector"


def test_embedder_empty_input():
    emb = get_embedder(settings.version("emb_v1"), backend="hash")
    assert emb.encode([]).shape == (0, settings.version("emb_v1").dim)


# ---- ingest (dry run) ----------------------------------------------------------

def test_ingest_dry_run_records_embedding_version():
    from retrieval.ingest import ingest

    manifest = ingest(str(REPO / "data" / "policies"), dry_run=True, backend="hash")
    assert manifest["n_chunks"] > 0
    assert manifest["n_docs"] == 2
    assert settings.active_version in manifest["embedding_versions"]
    ev = manifest["embedding_versions"][settings.active_version]
    assert ev["model_id"] and ev["dim"] == settings.version(settings.active_version).dim

    # manifest is the offline index_meta: it must be persisted and re-readable
    written = json.loads(Path(settings.ingest_manifest_path).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert written["active"] == settings.active_version
    assert written["dry_run"] is True


def test_estimate_tokens_monotonic():
    assert estimate_tokens("abcd") <= estimate_tokens("abcd" * 10)

PR1 is staged and working. Here's the state.

## What's staged (PR1 — retrieval ingest + index)

11 files, +888 lines, all additive — no existing source file touched:

- [retrieval/config.py](retrieval/config.py) — versioned embedding registry + env-overridable settings
- [retrieval/chunker.py](retrieval/chunker.py) — structure-first chunking on German `§`/`Teil` markers, token-budgeted window fallback; each chunk carries citation+filter metadata. (Fixed a real bug in the scaffold's window split: it sized windows in chars-as-words, ~7× too large, so oversized clauses never actually split — now derived from the text's own token density.)
- [retrieval/embedder.py](retrieval/embedder.py) — versioned embedder (model id + dim travel with vectors) + content-hash cache; BGE-M3 backend **plus** a deterministic, dependency-free `hash` backend for offline tests/CI
- [retrieval/index.py](retrieval/index.py) — Qdrant named-vector wrapper (two embedding versions coexist → sets up the PR4 zero-downtime migration)
- [retrieval/corpus.py](retrieval/corpus.py) + [retrieval/ingest.py](retrieval/ingest.py) — load → chunk → embed → upsert; records an `index_meta` manifest; degrades to manifest-only dry-run when Qdrant is down
- [data/policies/](data/policies/) — small illustrative German Kfz-Kasko + VVG corpus
- [tests/test_retrieval.py](tests/test_retrieval.py) — 8 offline tests, all passing

**Verified:** `EMBED_BACKEND=hash python -m retrieval.ingest --dry-run` → 14 chunks from 2 docs, manifest written with the embedding version recorded. Acceptance criteria from BUILD_PLAN PR1 met.

**Test honesty:** my 8 tests pass. The full suite still has 3 **pre-existing** failures in `tests/test_smoke.py` (prompt-length guard, a pillar-exclusion assertion, and an `ImportError` in `extraction/gemini_extractor.py`) — they're in code PR1 doesn't touch and fail identically without my changes. Not introduced here; worth a separate fix if you want.

Left untouched: `voice/livekit_agent.py` (your pre-existing edit), the WhatsApp image, and `echoclaim-spine/` (the planning scaffold that drives PR2–7).

## Commit message

```text
retrieval: add structure-aware ingest + Qdrant named-vector index (PR1)

Foundation for grounding Jamie's coverage answers in the policy corpus
instead of generating them.

- config: versioned embedding registry + env-overridable settings
- chunker: structure-first split on German § / Teil markers with a
  token-budgeted window fallback; chunks carry citation + filter
  metadata (clause_id, section_path, product_code, lang)
- embedder: model id + dim travel with the vectors; content-hash cache;
  BGE-M3 backend plus a deterministic hash backend for offline tests/CI
- index: Qdrant named vectors so two embedding versions can coexist
  (sets up the PR4 zero-downtime migration); payload indexes on filters
- corpus + ingest: load data/policies/*.md, chunk, embed, upsert; record
  an index_meta manifest; manifest-only dry run when Qdrant is absent
- data/policies: illustrative German Kfz-Kasko + VVG corpus
- tests: offline coverage of chunking, corpus, embedder, dry-run ingest

Run: EMBED_BACKEND=hash python -m retrieval.ingest --dry-run

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
```

I kept the `Co-Authored-By` trailer — honest attribution is the whole point of building it for real, and it costs you nothing in an interview where you can actually walk through the design.

Changes are staged but **not committed** (you only asked for the message + staged tree). Say the word and I'll commit, or move straight on to **PR2** (retriever + reranker + the `coverage_lookup` tool wired into the agent), which is where this starts paying off in the demo.
